products.title: Chombi Natural Geisha by the Altieri Family
products.body_html:
The newest Rare Release® is a contemporary classic from Panamanian coffee-producing powerhouse that proves legacies can still be built. 

Despite having ancient Ethiopian origins and a history of cultivation in Central America dating back to the 1950’s, the prestige of Panama Geisha has only fairly recently been realised after a geisha from Hacienda La Esmeralda won Best of Panama with an unprecedented score of 94 points in 2004. This groundbreaking moment put the varietal on the map and rightfully so—coffee had never before been as floral, as complex, or as expensive—and heralded a new wave of Panamanian coffee producers driven by stature and terroir expression. 

One of them was Eugene Altieri, who set up his estate in the Boquete highlands to produce some of the world's finest geisha coffees.

This lot, from their Mima Estate, is grown on the Chombi Block at the farm's highest elevations and is named for one of his grandchildren. The processing on this, their unique Dry Fermentation, is executed with Altieri's signature precision. Only ripe cherries are handpicked from dense and compact cherry clusters and left whole inside the harvest bags overnight to rest. In the morning they’re floated and spread out to dry on raised African beds for 5 days, then sealed in bags and fermented over 4 days. Final drying takes place in a refrigerated chamber over thirty days. 

Chombi offers easily our favourite geisha of the year with a dense and juicy cup profile—sticky tropical fruit notes of vanilla bean, mango, white peach and intense hibiscus florality all coated in a luxurious syrupy body.

This is a 48g jar from our Rare Release® category. It is roasted to order and will only be shipped as wholebean.

products.title: Imbalu Anaerobic Natural, Mount Elgon
products.body_html:
This anaerobic natural brings a feast of of blood orange, pinot noir, and black cherry. 

Processed by the roastery’s fave Ugandan producer Norman Mukuru this lot is a prime example of the bold, boozy, and expressive coffees he’s known for.  

Cherries brought in by local farmers were sorted and left to ferment as the people in the surrounding Mt Elgon area gathered for traditional Imbalu celebrations. During this time the coffee developed it’s sweet, wine-like intensity, after-which it was slowly dried for three weeks on raised beds.

products.title: Seasonal Capsules – Zebigi Washed
products.body_html:
The Coffee Gardens and 275 Ugandan growers deliver a delightful washed coffee that's crisp, elegant and kinda like tea. Find chamomile, Darjeeling, and red berries in our latest seasonal capsule release. 

The Ultimate Quick Guide to Capsule Brewer Husbandry:

  • Always purge your machine with a blank shot of water when switching between coffees
  • Give the pod a good shake
  • Let each cap warm up in the machine for 5-10" before starting the brew (this also helps improve the cap's seal)
  • By short we mean 32-35g in beverage weight (the default on your Nespresso® machine's small button should give you this – you may need to reset your machine if you've ever recorded over these settings)
  • Use your caps within 4 weeks/WKS and come back for more.

This run of pods is only available as a 10-unit refill pack. 

FAQ:

"Aren't capsules gross?" – yes, when the coffee going in is. And the same can be said for any brew method. Ever made a V60 with some incinerated supermarket beans? That'll set a new bar for gross.

"Will your Heirloom Blend be available in this format?" – try something new, live a little! But also, yes, someday, perhaps, possibly.

"Do you just grind your coffee and stick it in a pod?" – yes, but nope. The roasts sent to 4WKS are specifically roasted to extract well in the fast brew format of a capsule, and no that doesn't mean we roast darker for them. Aside from the work we do, the team at 4WKS rigorously test by refracting shots and calibrating grind settings to achieve taste and strength goals with each batch of coffee we supply. If it isn't hitting the right numbers, we start again.

"Why so expenny?" – not all coffees taste the same, and that's part of why they don't all cost the same. The lot going in to these caps isn't cheap, but truly great coffee never should be.

Send us more questions, we'll leave more answers.

products.title: Angelica Lopez Washed Caturra, Nueva Segovia
La Llama Coco Natural Geisha, Caranavi
products.body_html:
We've released PLUSMINUS ONE BILLION COFFEES this year. Among them were some of the most remarkable geishas we've ever tasted. Here's another 💅

Classy, captivating, and candy-like. This coco natural processed geisha comes from La Llama – a fog-blanketed, high-altitude farm in the mountain valley of Villa Rosario, Bolivia. 

Geisha cherries are shade-grown, handpicked at peak ripeness, and sorted before drying on patios for 48 to 72hrs. Once semi-dry, they're transferred to containers typically used for drying cacao pods, where a consistent flow of warm air and regular stirring slowly and evenly dries the beans over 55hrs.

The result is a complex cup that’s just lovely, no matter how it's brewed—lush stone-fruit filters, liquorice & coconut-ice espressos and sweet matcha milk drinks.
